text:
cs-elena: Acme support ticket — customers hitting 500s + streaming timeouts around 2026-03-18T14:11Z. Example req id: req_acme_0a9f3c. They're seeing spikes and retries, asking for an ETA.
incidents-bot: ALERT: 5xx spike on route hosted-gpu/us-west-2 between 14:09-14:15Z, p95 latency increased.
maya: grabbing logs from the pool now, can someone paste a sample req id and stderr?
cs-elena: linked req_acme_0a9f3c in ticket, logs show container exit code 139 then 500s.
sam: checking node pool metrics `kubectl get pods -n infer -l pool=hosted-gpu -o wide`
ops-bot: node gpu-11 reported OOM events at 14:11:50Z, container restart count incremented.
eng-reece: paste of container stderr from pod infer-runner-2345:
```
[14:11:49] infer-runner[2345]: runtime: attempting to allocate 768M
[14:11:50] kernel: python[2345]: segfault at 0 ip ... trace ...
[14:11:50] kubelet: Container exited with code 139, restarting
```
eng-ml: hypothesis: kv-prefetch + large context caused VRAM to balloon; long-context toolcall + QPS bump may have exceeded allocator limits.
cs-elena: customer notes: they sent ~180k token context + toolcall, concurrency ~9, and retried several times. Billing concerns raised.
maya: querying nvml telemetry: host gpu-11 VRAM usage ramped to 100% and nvml reported reset 14:11:51Z.
eng-reece: immediate mitigations proposed:
- throttle Acme org to 2rps at gateway (temp)
- route Acme traffic to cpu-fallback pool for toolcalls
- disable kv-prefetch on affected model route rdx-llm-7b-v2
oncall: implemented gateway rate-limit org:acme -> 2rps, ttl 45m, and applied route override to cpu-fallback pool.
maya: collecting coredump and docker events: running `kubectl exec -n infer debug-tool -- /usr/local/bin/collect-core req_acme_0a9f3c` -> uploading to s3://redwood-debug/acme/req_acme_0a9f3c.tgz
eng-ml: repro in staging (DO NOT RUN ON PROD w/o throttles):
```
# reproducer
for i in {1..10}; do \
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST \\
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
    -d '{"model":"rdx-llm-7b-v2","input":"<180k token context>\n<toolcall>","stream":false}' & \
  sleep 0.5
done
```
sam: reproduces OOM in ~60-120s at concurrency 7-10 when kv-prefetch enabled.
eng-reece: short-term rollback: revert runtime-qalloc-20260317 for rdx-llm-7b-v2 to runtime-20260310 (allocator differences suspected). Maya can toggle canary.
maya: canary flip started on 1 host to runtime-20260310 at 14:30Z, monitoring.
eng-ml: code change: add defensives to kv-prefetch — skip prefetch when ctx_tokens > 120k or batch_size > 6; force streaming mode for very long contexts. Draft PR #4210.
oncall: canary host stable for 10m, no 5xxs. Rolling hotfix plan pending.
cs-elena: informed customer of temporary throttles and route override; offered credit for failed requests, awaiting acceptance.
eng-reece: next actions:
- maya: complete cluster rollout back to previous runtime if canary stays healthy (ETA 30m)
- eng-ml: land PR #4210 and smoke tests (ETA 3h)
- sam: assemble NVML graphs + docker restart logs into incident binder (ETA 45m)
- oncall: keep throttles until postmortem complete
- cs-elena: hold customer comms and draft credit note
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE -> mitigated: 5xx rate dropped to baseline at 15:02Z after route changes and runtime canary.
maya: uploaded canary logs + coredump to s3://redwood-incidents/2026-03-18/acme-req_acme_0a9f3c.tgz
eng-ml: test harness simulates multi-tenant long-ctx backpressure; PR includes unit test and integration fixture.
eng-reece: root cause (preliminary): interaction between quantized allocator variant and aggressive kv-prefetch under high concurrency + oversized contexts -> unbounded device memory growth -> device reset -> process segfault -> 500s.
cs-elena: customer accepted credit, requested postmortem and timeline for permanent fix.
oncall: removed the temporary rate-limit at 15:25Z after full rollout; left cpu-fallback route active for 30m to be safe.
eng-reece: I'll lead postmortem and write RCA, include mem graphs, coredumps, PR refs, and rollout timeline.
cs-elena: thanks all :thumbsup: Closing CS ticket after postmortem and credit applied.
ops-bot: FINAL -> incident status: resolved. Follow-ups logged to incident board: add kv-prefetch guard, improve allocator telemetry, add per-org burst protection.
